overview: Bossiney Haven is a small, wild cove a mile east of Tintagel, reached down steep steps from the coast path. At low tide a sandy beach appears and links up with neighbouring Benoath Cove; at high tide the sea covers the sand completely.
It’s a place for explorers rather than deckchairs: towering cliffs, a huge sea cave and a natural arch called Elephant Rock, with the Iron Age cliff castle of Willapark on the headland above.

expect.title: Low-tide sand
expect.text: The beach only appears as the tide drops, when you can walk round to Benoath Cove next door.

expect.title: Caves and Elephant Rock
expect.text: On one side of the cove a cave around 60 feet high opens into a series of dark caverns, and nearby a tall arch has almost separated a ‘trunk’ of rock from the cliff.

expect.title: Clifftop walking
expect.text: The coast path runs right above the cove, with the Willapark headland and its Iron Age fort just to the north.

goodToKnow.label: Getting down
goodToKnow.text: Access is by steep steps, so it isn’t suitable for pushchairs or anyone unsteady on their feet.

goodToKnow.label: Tides
goodToKnow.text: The sand is completely covered at high tide, so check tide times and keep an eye on the incoming sea.

week.slot: An hour or two around low tide
week.text: Bossiney is a short, adventurous stop on a Tintagel day. Time it for low tide and combine it with the walk through Rocky Valley nearby.

pairWith.why: a dramatic ravine walk down to the sea
the legendary castle a mile away
a bigger sandy beach south of Tintagel

tips: Only go into the caves on a falling tide, and don’t get caught by the sea coming back in.
Wear shoes with grip for the steps.
